title: Project health: CI proves the build, robustness at the edges, painless onboarding
description:
Findings from a whole-repository audit (Rust crates, web app, Python analysis, CI, release, docs), grouped into four epics.

Purpose: make CI prove what the project already claims, harden the FFI and browser audio edges, and let a new contributor get a first sound out of a clean checkout on any platform.

Definition of done: every epic closed; CI builds the wasm crate, runs every existing test suite (Rust, wasm, web, Cucumber, pytest) and enforces rustfmt and clippy; a Linux checkout builds by following the README alone.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Suggested order, highest leverage first:

1. Epic apricitus-ad9efa (CI): wasm build and tests (apricitus-1f0e91), Cucumber conformance (apricitus-e83164), pytest/ruff/mypy (apricitus-8f7022), rustfmt/clippy/doc/audit (apricitus-2698fb).
2. Epic apricitus-634ee6 (analysis and onboarding): one-command setup on Linux (apricitus-446dba), Python packaging declares its imports (apricitus-ae920d).
3. Epic apricitus-1df421 (Rust): split the compiler and parser (apricitus-6372d1), then structured compile errors (apricitus-38a9a4).
4. Harden the edges: wasm FFI (apricitus-205813), analysis server (apricitus-fca129), browser audio failure paths (apricitus-5cb893, epic apricitus-0aa1f1).
5. License text and the Swift licensing decision (apricitus-874f56); release version bumps (apricitus-b799ab).

Everything else is independent and can be picked up in any order.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text: Project-management machinery: added .claude/hooks/session-start.sh, registered in .claude/settings.json, which installs the Kanbus CLI (kanbus + cffi from PyPI) in Claude Code on the web sessions. Verified by uninstalling kanbus and rerunning the hook. No separate issue per CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md.
